name: Fortunes Lost on Paper: Bubbles, Crashes and Panics
description: Tulips, Mississippi shares, railways and dot-coms: the stories of manias and crises, and what they teach about money and human hope.

checkpoints.name: The first manias
checkpoints.note: Silver floods into Europe and prices climb. In Holland people pay wild sums for tulips, and in France shares in the Mississippi Company soar and then collapse, teaching the hard way how a bubble ends.

checkpoints.name: Railways, gold and panics
checkpoints.note: Banks and railways spread across the world, and so do their panics. Gold rushes turn the hopeful into prospectors, while crises in 1837, 1857, 1873 and 1907 shake the United States.

checkpoints.name: Slump and inflation
checkpoints.note: German money turns to paper, and Wall Street crashes. The Great Depression follows, and governments take on the duty of managing the economy.

checkpoints.name: Global crises
checkpoints.note: Oil shocks, debt crises and bursting bubbles in Japan, Asia and the internet era lead up to the crash of 2008, when the fall of Lehman Brothers made the whole world's banks seem to shake at once.
